name: Ahmed Amhdour
intro: I’m Ahmed Amhdour, an AI Security Engineer focused on securing AI applications, RAG systems, and autonomous agents. My focus is protecting sensitive data, enforcing authorization, and keeping agent actions within clear security boundaries.

focus.title: Application security
focus.summary: Identity, ownership and access at the product boundary.

focus.title: Retrieval security
focus.summary: Keeping access permissions attached to information.

focus.title: Agent security
focus.summary: Bounding tool actions and delegated authority.

biography: I’m **Ahmed Amhdour**, a self-taught **AI Security Engineer** focused on securing AI applications, RAG systems, autonomous agents, and the infrastructure that connects them.
I’m also a **GITEX AFRICA 2026 Cyber & AI Achiever Award recipient — Rising Star (Individual)**, recognized in Marrakech for my work and direction in cybersecurity and AI security.

My focus is on understanding where **identity, sensitive data, retrieval, models, tools, agents, and external services cross trust boundaries**. I approach AI security through source-code analysis, threat modeling, controlled security labs, architecture tracing, adversarial testing, and reproducible evidence.
Rather than focusing on a single framework, I study security principles that transfer across modern AI systems.

projects.title: First Project — Enterprise AI Assistant Platform
paragraphs: I study the security of enterprise AI assistants that connect employees with organizational knowledge, language models, retrieval systems, and agent tools.

My work focuses on authentication and authorization, private conversations and files, secure document ingestion, RAG permissions, prompt injection, agent actions, MCP-style integrations, secrets, sandboxing, logging, supply-chain security, incident response, and secure deployment.
projects.summary: Security focus on identity, RAG permissions, prompt injection, and agent tools in enterprise AI assistants.

projects.title: Second Project — Self-Hosted AI Chat Platform
paragraphs: I study self-hosted AI applications that provide users with access to local and remote language models.

My security focus includes session security, user isolation, model-provider configuration, API-key protection, file uploads, tool permissions, prompt injection, sensitive-data exposure, logging, and deployment hardening.
projects.summary: Security focus on sessions, user isolation, API keys, uploads, and deployment hardening in self-hosted AI chat applications.

projects.title: Third Project — Private AI Knowledge Workspace
paragraphs: I study AI knowledge systems that ingest private documents and use retrieval-augmented generation to answer questions.

My focus includes document ownership, ingestion security, retrieval authorization, vector-search permissions, embedding privacy, indirect prompt injection, permission revocation, sensitive-data handling, retention, deletion, and secure multi-user access.
projects.summary: Security focus on document ownership, ingestion, retrieval authorization, privacy, and access revocation in private AI knowledge systems.

projects.title: Fourth Project — Multi-Provider AI Conversation Platform
paragraphs: I study AI platforms that connect users with multiple models, providers, tools, and external services through a common application.

My security work focuses on identity, API authorization, provider credentials, conversation privacy, uploaded content, model routing, tool permissions, external integrations, logging, output handling, and preventing untrusted AI-generated content from becoming trusted authority.
projects.summary: Security focus on provider credentials, conversation privacy, model routing, tool permissions, and untrusted output across AI integrations.

approach.title: My Security Engineering Approach
approach.focusLead: Across these systems, I concentrate on the security problems that remain important regardless of the underlying technology:
approach.evidence: I want security conclusions to be based on evidence rather than assumptions. I therefore distinguish between source analysis, planned experiments, controlled lab results, independently demonstrated work, and real production experience.
approach.goal: My goal is to help build AI systems where **data access is intentional, agent authority is constrained, actions are independently authorized, failures are observable, and security claims can be demonstrated with evidence.**
